questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bangladesh?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bangladesh article.

questions.proof: Dhaka is the capital and the biggest city.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Bangladesh?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Bangladesh on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bangladesh article.

questions.proof: Bangladesh has land borders with India on the north, west, and east, and Myanmar on the southeast.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In the north, the Siliguri Corridor separates it from _____ and Nepal, and the Indian state of Sikkim separates it from China.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Nepal”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bangladesh article.

questions.proof: In the north, the Siliguri Corridor separates it from Bhutan and Nepal, and the Indian state of Sikkim separates it from China.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The _____ military refused to give power to the Awami League, led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “military”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bangladesh article.

questions.proof: The Pakistan military refused to give power to the Awami League, led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “On 16 December _____, Pakistan surrendered, and Bangladesh became independent after a 9-month war.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
